audit.why: Vladimir bullies the melee, mana-bound Kassadin all lane; Kassadin's threat is scaling and roams, not winning stages. Matches 51.05% Vlad WR over 2153 games.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart said Skill on all seven rows while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart say Vladimir on all seven; several full whys (e.g. 'your level 1 is among the worst mid') argued against the content verdict.
audit.why: Two layers rendered opposite answers; content and packet agree Vladimir holds every stage when played correctly.
audit.corrected: All seven full sides moved to Vladimir, whys rewritten pro-Vladimir and grounded in the kits.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content called Kassadin's Q a 'silence' twice (spikes[1].text, mid) — current Null Sphere interrupts channels, it does not silence. whys[1] claimed his Q shield 'can't stop your Transfusion' — it is a magic-damage shield and does absorb it. breakdown.cooldowns had no digits; two Do's/Don'ts bodies were tradeGood/tradeBad verbatim.
audit.why: Riot's Q text: 'interrupting channels... shield that absorbs magic damage'. Riftwalk is 5/3.5/2s CD, W is a 7s auto-reset (the burst tell flagged in missingInteractions), his E is 21-17s.
audit.corrected: Silence wording replaced with QW burst, shield claim corrected to its short duration vs your costless Q, cooldowns field now carries Riftwalk/W numbers plus the W wind-up tell, bleed bullets rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere.
audit.why: Riftwalk numbers and the commit-after-he-blinks rule now live in breakdown.cooldowns and dontsFull[2].d.

edits.before: Kassadin wins by landing Riftwalk, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Kassadin wins by farming safely to 6, then Riftwalk-roaming for kills you can't match and out-scaling the lane you never punished.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Kassadin Riftwalk: 5s base at rank 1, 2s max — cheap once, mana-hungry stacked; commit only after he blinks in. - His W auto-reset wind-up is your step-back cue, not the cast. - Your W pool: the moment it goes wrong. - The R: the moment it goes right.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: His Q shield only blocks magic briefly and costs 60+ mana — your Q costs nothing, so the chip war is yours.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: Riftwalk is a 500-range blink on a 5s base cooldown at 6 — past river with W down you hand him the free all-in.

edits.after: Vladimir

edits.before: Q-farm and nothing else — your level 1 is among the worst mid. Give CS you can't Q safely and smile about it.
edits.after: He is melee with no gap-closer pre-6 — E-charge and Q him at 600 range every time he steps to a last hit.

edits.after: Vladimir

edits.before: Still surviving. Q on cooldown when free, pool saved for the jungler you haven't seen yet.
edits.after: Keep chipping: your Q costs nothing, his answers cost mana. Pool stays saved for the gank.

edits.after: Vladimir

edits.before: E charges join the pattern: Q-E wave contact trades start mattering. Health is your mana — spend like an accountant.
edits.after: Charged E plus Q on every walk-up — his Q shield blunts one hit and melee CS costs him health he can't heal back.

edits.after: Crimson Rush windows: empowered Q chunks and heals while he is still farming at your feet — the lead grows.

edits.after: Vladimir

edits.before: Hemoplague online — the all-in inverts: Q-E-R-E with ignite kills most mids who thought they were winning.
edits.after: His 6 is the danger point, but a built HP lead plus Hemoplague still wins — pool the blink follow-up, then R.

edits.after: Riftmaker keeps you ahead of his curve: every trade heals more than it costs while he is still stacking mana.

edits.before: Late Vlad is a raid boss: pool their engage, R their clump, and drain whatever stayed to argue.
edits.after: Kept behind, he stays behind: pool his blink engage, R the clump, and out-live his one-target burst.

edits.before: Level 2 his magic-only Q shield can't stop your Transfusion chunks.
edits.after: Level 2 his brief Q shield costs mana; your costless Q outlasts it.

edits.before: Kassadin spikes with R Riftwalk, but Hemoplague plus your accumulated HP lead means you still win the trade. When he blinks in, pool his Q silence follow-up and burst him with R plus charged E before his RW-RE combo lands. Don't let him free-farm to stack Riftwalk; keep shoving so he can't roam safely.
edits.after: Kassadin spikes with R Riftwalk, but Hemoplague plus your accumulated HP lead means you still win the trade. When he blinks in, pool his Q-W burst follow-up and hit him with R plus charged E before his RW-RE combo lands. Don't let him free-farm to stack Riftwalk; keep shoving so he can't roam safely.

edits.before: Even at his level 6 R Riftwalk spike your HP lead and Hemoplague win the trade; pool his Q silence and burst him before RW-RE. Keep shoving so he can't roam or stack safely.
edits.after: Even at his level 6 R Riftwalk spike your HP lead and Hemoplague win the trade; pool his Q-W burst and kill before RW-RE. Keep shoving so he can't roam or stack safely.

notes: Chart: full layer flipped to Vladimir on all seven rows to match content win[] and the packet; a clean sweep for the owner is unusual but both authoritative layers agree and the kit supports it (melee, mana-bound, no pre-6 gap-closer vs costless 600-range poke). Kassadin's Q has not silenced since his rework — it interrupts channels; two content fields said 'silence' and were corrected. 'ahead', breakdown.carry/feeding/wave remain structurally templated; nothing Kassadin-specific verifiable to add at length without inventing.
